cultural.vision_reason: This is a New Kingdom (Amarna period) sunk-relief talatat block depicting Queen Nefertiti in profile, from a temple at Karnak — genuine ancient Egyptian temple relief sculpture made in Egypt.

physical.title: Talatat: Portrait of Nefertiti
physical.summary: The son of Amenhotep III, Akenhaten, brought about the short-lived "monotheistic" revolution in Egyptian religion near the end of Dynasty 18. The young king constructed a temple complex to the Aten, the Sun Disk, at Karnak—from which this relief comes—before he moved his capital to El Amarna. For reasons yet unknown, the figure of the Queen Nefertiti appears in these reliefs far more often that that of the king. Ironically, the Aten temples were dismantled to be used as foundations and fill for additions to the Great Temple of Amun, whom the Aten had briefly displaced.

location.made_in_place: Egypt, Karnak, New Kingdom (1540–1069 BCE), Dynasty 18, reign of Akhenaten (1351–1334 BCE)
